clue.text: Fine in country bordering sea, balmy

indicators.note: one thing set in another is enclosed by it, so the fine abbreviation goes inside the country

blocks.note: a South American country
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
the Med, short for the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: A traveller describes a fine day in a coastal country with balmy weather.
explanation.walkthrough: PER(F)U is followed by MED: 'bordering' just places the sea beside the country. 'Balmy' looks like weather but means sweet-smelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Balmy can mean fragrant like balm, so something perfumed is scented in that way.

clue.text: Noble gong for little flapper?

blocks.note: an earl is a nobleman
a gong is slang for a medal or honour, such as the OBE (Order of the British Empire)

explanation.surface: An aristocrat is awarded an honour, apparently for a 1920s flapper girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flapper' suggests a 1920s party girl, but the little flapper is the soft dangling part of an ear.
explanation.definitionFit: The earlobe is the small fleshy part that hangs and can flap at the bottom of the ear, a playful description.

clue.text: Nemesis of the 22 character, anything but canny Scottish PM?

blocks.note: canny in the Scottish sense means careful with money; flash means showy and extravagant, its opposite
Gordon Brown, the Scottish-born UK Prime Minister

explanation.surface: A cartoon villain's foe is likened to a Scottish prime minister who is anything but shrewd.
explanation.walkthrough: 22 is MERCILESS: Ming the Merciless is the villain of the Flash Gordon comics and films, and Flash is his enemy.
explanation.definitionFit: Flash Gordon is the space hero who repeatedly defeats the tyrant Ming the Merciless, his arch-enemy.

clue.text: See 16
Actor redoing short plays

indicators.note: something short is missing its end, so the final letter is dropped
to play with letters is to move them about into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An actor is redoing short plays, perhaps reviving one-act dramas.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert De Niro is an American film actor famous for Taxi Driver and Raging Bull.

clue.text: Brick dropped softly onto Russian

blocks.note: Misha is a Russian man's name, a familiar form of Mikhail
p for piano, the musical instruction to play softly

explanation.surface: A brick is dropped gently onto a Russian man, perhaps on a building site.
explanation.walkthrough: To drop a brick is a British idiom for making a tactless blunder, so 'Brick dropped' means a gaffe, not falling masonry.
explanation.definitionFit: A mishap is an unlucky accident or blunder, which is what a dropped brick in the idiomatic sense amounts to.

clue.text: Punish explanation originally penned by solicitor: it's beyond me!

definitions.note: mete out means to hand out a punishment; the clue's verb stands for the whole act

indicators.note: something penned is shut in a pen, so this letter is enclosed by the next word
originally points at the first letter of the word just before it, picked out to join the others
beyond means further along, so this part follows the pronoun in the answer

blocks.note: taken as written
a tout solicits custom, for example selling tickets
the opening letter of explanation

explanation.surface: A solicitor's explanation of a punishment is beyond the speaker's understanding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solicitor' looks like a lawyer but here is someone touting for trade, like a ticket tout.
explanation.definitionFit: To mete out is to dispense or administer, used chiefly of punishment, so it serves as punishing.

clue.text: Insignificant litre in whisky, I'm opening case of sake!

indicators.note: one thing set in another is enclosed by it, so the litre abbreviation goes inside the whisky
something opening a case prises it apart and sits within it
the case of a word is its outside, so only its first and last letters are kept

blocks.note: the first and last letters of sake
malt is a type of whisky
L is the abbreviation for litre
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A tiny measure of whisky slipped into a crate of sake is a trivial matter.
explanation.walkthrough: Malt whisky is the drink meant; the case of sake is just its first and last letters, wrapped round everything else.
explanation.definitionFit: Small-time describes someone or something minor and unimportant, which is what insignificant means.

clue.text: Wee bairns in kilt and bra seen drunk

indicators.note: a drunk person staggers about, so these letters are jumbled out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Small Scottish children dressed in a kilt and bra are spotted tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: A bairn is a Scottish word for a child; 'in' and 'and' are joining words, not part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Ankle-biters is jokey slang for small children, who are about knee-high, matching the Scots for little kids.

clue.text: Mention ornament in conversation?

indicators.note: in conversation means spoken out loud, so we want a word that sounds the same as another

blocks.note: a brooch is a decorative pin, an ornament

explanation.surface: Someone raises the subject of a piece of jewellery while chatting.
explanation.definitionFit: To broach a subject is to raise it for discussion, that is, to mention it.

clue.text: Never a player for rejection

blocks.note: never in the sense of not at all
Tom Hanks, the actor; a player is an actor

explanation.surface: A casting note: never pick a certain player, as a rejection.
explanation.definitionFit: 'No thanks' is the stock phrase of polite refusal, a rejection of an offer.

clue.text: Noxious thing, beastly girl, stinker

indicators.note: something noxious is foul and poisoned, so these letters are corrupted into another order

blocks.note: taken as written
a mare is a female horse, a girl among beasts

explanation.surface: A string of insults aimed at some unpleasant young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noxious thing' reads like an insult, but noxious tells us to rearrange the word thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A stinker is something very unpleasant or difficult, and a nightmare is a dreadful experience or situation.

clue.text: Adamant over hanging that proved divisive for some time

definitions.text: that proved divisive for some time

blocks.note: iron, as in an iron will, is unyielding
a curtain is a hanging drape

explanation.surface: Someone adamant about hanging something, a matter that long caused division.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' just puts the first piece above the second in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iron Curtain was the Cold War boundary that divided Europe into East and West for decades.

clue.text: Ballet dancer shaves back

indicators.note: going back means travelling the opposite way, so the word is read from end to start

blocks.note: to peel is to shave off a thin layer

explanation.surface: A male ballet dancer shaves his back.
explanation.walkthrough: Wayne Sleep is a well-known British ballet dancer, formerly of the Royal Ballet.
explanation.definitionFit: Wayne Sleep is a famous British ballet dancer, so his surname stands for the dancer.

clue.text: Change done after altering shape

indicators.note: altering something changes its arrangement, so these letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A change is done once something has been altered into shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A hendecagon is a geometric figure with eleven sides, a kind of polygon or shape.

clue.text: Capital too far out in Scotland

blocks.note: OTT means over the top, going too far
awa is Scots for away, that is, out

explanation.surface: A capital city lies much too far out, somewhere in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Ottawa is the capital city of Canada.

clue.text: Explosion of myth has nailed leader in error over Partygate, domestic function — a juvenile excuse

indicators.note: an explosion blows things apart, so the following word's letters are scattered and reassembled
to nail something is to pin it down, holding it between the reworked letters
in a down answer one piece placed over another simply comes before it
the leader of a word is its front, so only its opening letter is taken

blocks.note: taken as written
leader of error is its first letter
a party is a do, followed by gate as written
domestic means relating to home
a function is a job or task, what something does as work

explanation.surface: A political row over Partygate has nailed a myth, the leader's excuses dismissed as childish.
explanation.walkthrough: Partygate was the 2021-22 UK scandal over parties held at Downing Street during Covid lockdowns; 'party' here is just a do.
explanation.definitionFit: Claiming the dog ate my homework is the classic lame excuse a schoolchild gives for not handing in work.

clue.text: Content to leave grand-niece with baby twins

indicators.note: when the contents leave, only the outside shell remains, so just the end letters stay

blocks.note: the first and last letters of grand-niece
baby as an adjective means miniature, mini

explanation.surface: A relative is happy to leave her grand-niece with a baby to look after.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content' looks like 'happy', but it means the inside of the word that follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Gemini is the zodiac sign of the Twins, Castor and Pollux.

clue.text: Fruity thing, like a US pop diva?

blocks.note: first meaning: a small stone fruit
second meaning, a jokey coinage: resembling the singer Cher

explanation.walkthrough: Cher is the American pop diva; adding the adjective ending to her name makes 'Cher-ry', like Cher.
explanation.definitionFit: The cherry is a small red stone fruit, and the punning adjective describes something resembling the singer Cher.

clue.text: Stick poster on this page?

blocks.note: an ad, a poster advertisement
here means in this very place

explanation.surface: An instruction to stick a poster onto this page.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to stick fast to a surface.

clue.text: As an agent shown by male cutting flesh up

definitions.note: behalf is a noun used in 'on behalf of', meaning as agent for

indicators.note: something cutting into another goes inside it
in a down answer going up means read from bottom to top

blocks.note: flab is excess flesh
he, the male pronoun

explanation.surface: An agent is exposed as a man carving meat.
explanation.walkthrough: FLA(HE)B is read upwards in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting on someone's behalf means acting as their representative or agent.

clue.text: Caught man?

blocks.note: c for caught, the cricket scoring abbreviation
a man is a chess piece, such as the rook

explanation.surface: Is this man the one who was caught?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a criminal is the sort of man who gets caught.
explanation.definitionFit: A crook is a criminal, the kind of man who ends up being caught by police.

clue.text: Cruel, 10 to the French?

blocks.note: 10 across is a two-word phrase of refusal; its thanks in French is merci, and 'no' becomes the ending less

explanation.surface: Is it cruel to answer the French with a cross-reference?
explanation.walkthrough: Turning down thanks gives thankless; doing it in French gives merci-less.
explanation.definitionFit: Merciless means showing no pity, which is what cruel describes.

clue.text: Bug in flower over mountain, reportedly?

indicators.note: reportedly means as told by word of mouth, so a sound-alike word is wanted

blocks.note: molten rock flows down over a volcano, so it is a flower over a mountain

explanation.surface: An insect is found in a bloom on a hillside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' means something that flows, not a bloom. In non-rhotic British speech the two words sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A larva is the grub stage of an insect, and a bug is an informal word for an insect.

clue.text: See 2
Not entirely elliptic, as an oval stud

indicators.note: not entirely means only part of the following words is used, a run of letters inside them

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of the first word into the start of the last

explanation.surface: A shape is described as nearly elliptical, like an oval stud earring.
explanation.definitionFit: Casanova was the notorious Venetian seducer, so his name is used for any womaniser or stud.

clue.text: See 3
See 6
Something added by queen that's wrong, leader in error

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its front, so only its first letter is taken

blocks.note: Queen Anne, British monarch
a cross marks something wrong
the first letter of error

explanation.surface: A queen's addition turns out to be wrong, the result of a mistake at the top.
explanation.definitionFit: An annexe is an extension or supplementary building added on to a main one.

clue.text: Bouts of laughter around intimate creative expression

indicators.note: one thing around another surrounds it

blocks.note: fits of laughter
near as in close, intimate

explanation.surface: Fits of laughter surround a moment of intimate artistic expression.
explanation.definitionFit: The fine arts, such as painting and sculpture, are forms of creative expression.
